--- title: "eegSeminaR Notes" author: "Daniel Soto" --- These are my notes and completed exercises taken from [this 2022 seminar on EEG data analysis in R](https://alexenge.github.io/eegSeminaR/). Citation: > Enge A (2023). eegSeminaR: A Seminar on Analyzing EEG Data in R. https://github.com/alexenge/eegSeminaR, https://alexenge.github.io/eegSeminaR/. ## Setting Up Data Though they use the data at `alexenge/erpcore`, we will be downloading the data using the `osfr` package, as the `erpcore` R package seems to be broken. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pak::pak("osfr") library(osfr) library(here) # For general handling of local data files ``` ::: Moreover, we will only be using data from the N170 experiment, which showed that subjects who were hooked up to EEGs and were tasked with viewing faces elicited different responses than when they were tasked to view cars. We use the `osfr` package to get the data in BIDS format. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bids_dir <- here("eegs", "data/n170") dir.create(bids_dir, recursive = TRUE) # Connect to the N170 OSF project n170_osf <- osf_retrieve_node("https://osf.io/pfde9/") # See the top-level folders folders <- osf_ls_files(n170_osf, n_max = Inf) folders # Get the folder with data in BIDS format bids_folder <- folders[ folders$name == "N170 Raw Data BIDS-Compatible", ] bids_folder bids_files <- osf_ls_files( bids_folder, n_max = Inf ) osf_download( bids_files, path = bids_dir, conflicts = "overwrite", recurse = TRUE ) ``` ::: ## Preprocessing For preprocessing, we first load `eegUtils`, a package for working with EEG data. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pak::pak("craddm/eegUtils") library(eegUtils) ``` ::: The downloaded ERP CORE data is in `data/n170`, as we specified in the setup section. The data is in BIDS format; though the seminar notes say the subjects are each in their respective `sub-XXX/egg` directory, on my end the file structure looks like `{subject-number}/{subject-number}_N170.set`. So, we retrieve this `.set` file for subject 1: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bids_dir <- here("eegs", "data/n170") set_file <- here(bids_dir, "sub-001/eeg/sub-001_task-N170_eeg.set") file.exists(set_file) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ::: `eegUtils` has functions for importing raw EEG data from various file formats into R, including the `.set` format used by ERP CORE. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Needed these packages for `import_set` to work pak::pak("R.matlab", "hdf5r") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_raw <- import_set(set_file) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Importing from EEGLAB .set file. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Importing data from .fdt file. ``` ::: ::: Inspecting the data type: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} class(dat_raw) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "eeg_data" ``` ::: ::: we see `eeg_data` is a custom class defined by participant_id: chr "sub-001_task-N170_eeg" ..$ recording : chr "sub-001_task-N170_eeg" $ version :Classes 'package_version', 'numeric_version' hidden list of 1 ..$ : int [1:3] 0 8 0 - attr(*, "class")= chr "eeg_data" ``` ::: ::: The data we actually care about is in the `dat_raw$signals` data frame. Here, each row is one sample (time point), each column is one channel (EEG electrode), and each value is the EEG voltage (in microvolts; µV) measured at this time sample and channel. ### Viewing Data We can visually check the data at multiple steps using the `browse_data` function. This will open a site we can open either on our browser or in the "Viewer" tab on the right-hand side of RStudio from which we can interactively inspect the data. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} browse_data(dat_raw) ``` ::: We can also make a static butterfly plot of a given chunk of data: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} time_lim <- c(300, 305) plot_butterfly(dat_raw, time_lim, baseline = time_lim) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Baseline: 300 - 305s ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](eeg-seminar_files/figure-html/butterfly-plot-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### Channel Locations For some steps, such as with making topographic plots, we need to know the relative positions of electrodes on the scalp. These are sometimes included in the raw data, but in this case we need to use a separate function: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_raw <- electrode_locations(dat_raw, montage = "biosemi64", overwrite = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Electrodes not found: HEOG_left HEOG_right VEOG_lower ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} dat_raw$chan_info ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 33 × 9 electrode radius theta phi cart_x cart_y cart_z x y 1 FP1 1 -92 -72 -26.2 80.8 -2.97 -28.4 87.5 2 F3 1 -60 -51 -46.3 57.2 42.5 -37.8 46.6 3 F7 1 -92 -36 -68.7 49.9 -2.97 -74.4 54.1 4 FC3 1 -50 -28 -57.5 30.6 54.6 -44.2 23.5 5 C3 1 -46 0 -61.1 0 59.0 -46 0 6 C5 1 -69 0 -79.4 0 30.5 -69 0 7 P3 1 -60 51 -46.3 -57.2 42.5 -37.8 -46.6 8 P7 1 -92 36 -68.7 -49.9 -2.97 -74.4 -54.1 9 P9 1 -115 36 -62.3 -45.3 -35.9 -93.0 -67.6 10 PO7 1 -92 54 -49.9 -68.7 -2.97 -54.1 -74.4 # ℹ 23 more rows ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot_electrodes(dat_raw, interact = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: Ignoring 3 observations ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Re-referencing During recording ("online"), each electrode is measuring the difference in voltage compared to the reference electrode (e.g., FCz). In contrast, during preprocessing ("offline"), a new reference is typically chose: - **Average reference**: Difference to the average of all scalp channels - **Linked mastoids**: Difference to the average of the mastoid channels (M1 and M2) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} eog_channels <- c("HEOG_left", "HEOG_right", "VEOG_lower") dat_reref <- eeg_reference(dat_raw, ref_chans = "average", exclude = eog_channels) ``` ::: ### Filtering We now want to filter our signals for frequencies that represent brain waves, and nothing else. According to the seminar's notes, the kinds of wave frequencies that we will encounter will represent the following EEG activity: Frequency | EEG activity --- | --- < 0.1 Hz | Electrode drift, sweat artifacts 0.1–4 Hz (delta) | Slow-wave sleep 4–8 Hz (theta) | Drowsiness, idling 8–13 Hz (alpha) | Relaxing, inhibition 13–30 Hz (beta) | Active thinking, alertness 30–80 Hz (gamma) | Binding, consciousness (?) 50 Hz (US: 60 Hz) | Power line noise \> 80 Hz | Muscle artifacts Thus, we only really care about the waves with frequencies between 0.1 Hz and 30 Hz. To remove unwanted parts of the signal, we do the following: 1. Convert time-domain EEG into the frequency domain via Fourier Transform 2. Remove or attenuate certain frequencies, depending on whether they are in our range or not. - A *high-pass* filter will remove slow frequencies (in our case, <0.1 Hz) - A *low-pass* filter will remove fast frequencies (in our case, >30 Hz) - A *band-pass* filter combines a high-pass and low-pass filter - A *band-stop* filter removes a narrow frequency range (e.g. around 50 Hz) 3. Convert cleaned signal back into the time domain This can all be done with one function, `eeg_filter`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_filt <- eeg_filter(dat_reref, low_freq = 0.1, high_freq = 30.0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Band-pass FIR filter from 0.1 - 30 Hz ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Transition bandwidth: 0.1 Hz ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Filter order: 33792 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Removing channel means... ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot_butterfly(dat_filt, time_lim, baseline = time_lim) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Baseline: 300 - 305s ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](eeg-seminar_files/figure-html/filtering-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: Let's now save our preprocessed data: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} deriv_dir <- here(bids_dir, "derivatives/eegUtils/sub-001/eeg") preproc_file <- here(deriv_dir, "sub-001_task-N170_desc-preprocessed_eeg.rds") dir.create(deriv_dir, recursive = TRUE) saveRDS(dat_filt, preproc_file) ``` ::: ### Extra: Downsampling The **sampling rate** is the number of EEG voltages recorded per second (in Hz). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_raw$srate ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1024 ``` ::: ::: This means that each pair of samples is less than 1 ms apart: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} 1 / dat_raw$srate ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.0009765625 ``` ::: ::: We don't need that much temporal resolution, so we will downsample the data using `eeg_downsample` from the `eegUtils` library: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_downs <- eeg_downsample(dat_filt, q = 4.0) # q is the downsampling factor ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Downsampling from 1024Hz to 256Hz. ``` ::: ::: This will reduce our computer's memory load and make subsequent computations faster: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} show_size_mb <- function(x) format(object.size(x), units = "MB") lapply(list(before = dat_filt, after = dat_downs), show_size_mb) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` $before [1] "184.1 Mb" $after [1] "46.1 Mb" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} saveRDS(dat_downs, preproc_file) ``` ::: ## Creating Epochs ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} deriv_dir <- here(bids_dir, "derivatives/eegUtils/sub-001/eeg") ``` ::: ### Event Codes Significant "events," (e.g. stimuli, responses) are marked in the EEG recording by unique **event codes**. In this experiment, event codes between 1-40 mean the stimulus was a face, while event codes between 41-80 mean the stimulus was a car. Note that in my case, the `task-N170_events.json` file did not exist in the directory where the N170 data got downloaded, but that is ok because we still know from the paper that this convention was used. We can hard-code these events as epoch labels as follows: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} event_codes <- c(1:80) epoch_labels <- ifelse(event_codes <= 40, "face", "car") ``` ::: ### Construct Epochs Now, knowing event codes, we can "cut out" our epochs around them. For the epoch data, we want to include between 100-200 ms before the stimulus onset as a baseline period. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_epo <- epoch_data( dat_downs, event_codes, time_lim = c(-0.2, 0.8), epoch_labels = epoch_labels ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Adjusting output limits to match sampling rate. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Output limits: -0.19921875 0.80078125 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` No baseline removal performed. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Creating 160 epochs. ``` ::: ::: To plot these epochs, we use an "ERP image," with: - X-axis: Time relative to stimulus onset - Y-axis: Trial number (or any other sorting, e.g. by reaction time) - Colors: EEG amplitude ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} erp_image(dat_epo, electrode = "PO8", smoothing = 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](eeg-seminar_files/figure-html/erp-image-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### Baseline Correction Trials will differ in their overall amplitude, i.e. due to drifts and slow artifacts. This can hide more subtle differences between conditions. The solution to this is to subtract the average activity during the pre-stimulus baseline: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_basl <- rm_baseline(dat_epo, c(-0.2, 0.0)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Baseline: -0.2 - 0s ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} erp_image(dat_basl, electrode = "PO4", smoothing = 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](eeg-seminar_files/figure-html/remove-baseline-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: We can confirm that the average voltage during the baseline window is actually zero given an epoch and channel: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Extract baseline time points (baseline meaning before onset, thus t < 0.0) at # epoch 42 inds <- which(dat_basl$timings$epoch == 42 & dat_basl$timings$time < 0.0) mean(dat_basl$signals$FP1[inds]) # close enough to 0 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 5.04796e-16 ``` ::: ::: Now, we can save the baseline-corrected epochs. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} epo_file <- here(deriv_dir, "sub-001_task-N170_desc-epoched_eeg.rds") saveRDS(dat_basl, epo_file) ``` ::: ## Removing Artifacts ### Independent Component Analysis With the baseline-corrected epoch data, we can run Independent Component Analysis (ICA) to separate our EEG recordings into a number of additive sub-components. The seminar decides to separate into the 15 most important components: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} n_components <- 15 ica <- run_ICA(dat_epo, method = "fastica", pca = n_components) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Reducing data to 15 dimensions using PCA. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Running fastica (ica). ``` ::: ::: With this, we can plot scalp distributions of the extracted ICA components. In particular, eye-blink and vertical eye movement components will have a very strong signal at the forehead (`Comp001``Comp001`), and vertical eye movement components will have opposite polarities left-frontal vs. right-frontal (maybe `Comp008` and/or `Comp009`). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} topoplot( ica, component = 1:n_components, limits = c(-20, 20), chan_marker = "none", scaling=0.4 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Plotting 15 components ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Using electrode locations from data. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Removing channels with no location. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Plotting head r 95 mm ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](eeg-seminar_files/figure-html/ica-topoplot-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: We can also automatically detect "bad" components based on their correlation with the electrooculogram (EOG), the part that measures eye-movement signals. We set a threshold of `0.6`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} heog <- c("HEOG_left", "HEOG_right") veog <- c("FP2", "VEOG_lower") bad_components <- ar_eogcor(ica, dat_epo, heog, veog, threshold = 0.6) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](eeg-seminar_files/figure-html/eog-corr-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Components with high EOG correlation: Comp001 Comp006 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} bad_components ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Comp001" "Comp006" ``` ::: ::: Weirdly, in the seminar, it ends up being components 001 and 009 that are outliers, but here we see we get components 001 and 006 are the outliers. I chalk this up to the potential differences that may have come from us using different R package sources for the data we use. Regardless, with this, we can remove the "bad" ICA components from the actual (epoched) data: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_icacorr <- apply_ica(dat_epo, ica, comps = bad_components) ``` ::: The seminar provides useful helper functions to compare the uncorrected and corrected epochs visually: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} extract_epoch <- function(epochs, epoch_no, electrode) { epoch_ixs <- epochs$timings$epoch == epoch_no data.frame( time = unique(epochs$timings$time), amplitude = epochs$signals[epoch_ixs, electrode][[1]] ) } compare_epochs <- function(uncorr_epochs, corr_epochs, epoch_no, electrode) { require(ggplot2) n_samples <- length(unique(uncorr_epochs$timings$time)) epochs <- list(uncorr_epochs, corr_epochs) |> lapply(extract_epoch, epoch_no, electrode) |> do.call(what = "rbind") epochs$type <- rep(c("uncorrected", "corrected"), each = n_samples) |> factor(levels = c("uncorrected", "corrected")) ggplot(epochs, aes(x = time, y = amplitude, color = type)) + geom_line() + labs(x = "Time (s)", y = "Amplitude (µV)", color = NULL) + ggtitle(paste0("Epoch #", epoch_no, ", channel ", electrode)) + theme_minimal() } compare_epochs(dat_epo, dat_icacorr, epoch_no = 103, electrode = "FP1") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Loading required package: ggplot2 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](eeg-seminar_files/figure-html/bad-comp-removal-visual-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### Artifact Rejection ICA may not be able to correct all eye movements or other artifacts. Additionally, we want to reject all epochs where at least one channel exceeds an absolute voltage thresheld, like ±100 µV. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_rej <- ar_thresh(dat_icacorr, threshold = c(100, -100), reject = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` 1175 (0.09%) samples above 100 uV threshold. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` 546 (0.04%) samples below -100 uV threshold. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` 18 epochs contain samples above threshold. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Removing 18 epochs. ``` ::: ::: Thresholds in practice should be chosen carefully, as rejecting many epochs reduces statistical power. More sophisticated thresholding approaches exist, e.g. via a moving window. Save artifact-corrected epochs for later: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} corr_file <- here(deriv_dir, "sub-001_task-N170_desc-corrected_eeg.rds") saveRDS(dat_rej, corr_file) ``` ::: ## Extracting Amplitudes ### Selecting Region of Interest We can't just measure a single EEG electrode. For one thing, single measurements are noisy and spatially imprecise. Thus, averaging across nearby electrodes boosts our signal-to-noise ratio. For another, their measurements are not well-defined without relationships to other electrodes. Altogether, this leads to us defining the **region of interest (ROI)**, "the set of electrodes where we expect our ERP component of interest to be maximal." First, we convert our epoched data to a data frame for subsetting / averages. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_frame <- as.data.frame(dat_epo) str(dat_frame) ``` ::: {.cell-output ... $ recording : chr "sub-001_task-N170_eeg" "sub-001_task-N170_eeg" "sub-001_task-N170_eeg" "sub-001_task-N170_eeg" ... $ event_type : num 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 ... $ epoch_labels : chr "car" "car" "car" "car" ... ``` ::: ::: Now, we know from prior N170 research that the face-sensitive N170 is strongest over bilateral posterior-occipitotemporal scalp, so we'll summarize the EEG from the six electrodes covering that region: | Left Hemisphere | Right Hemisphere | | ---- | ----- | | P7 | P8 | | P9 | P10 | | PO7 | PO8 | In particular, we have - P7, P8 = left/right parietal - P9, P10 = farther lateral/inferior left/right posterior sites - PO7, PO8 = left/right parieto-occipital With this, we create a new "virtual" channel, a column in the data frame, containing the average signal in the ROI: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} roi <- c("P7", "P8", "P9", "P10", "PO7", "PO8") dat_frame$roi <- rowMeans(dat_frame[roi]) ``` ::: ### Select Time Window ERP components unfold on the time scale of 10 ms to multiples 100s of ms. Here, we want to select the time window for where we expect our component to be — in our case, around 170 ms for the N170. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tmin <- 0.15 tmax <- 0.2 dat_frame <- subset(dat_frame, time >= tmin & time < tmax) ``` ::: Averaging across this time window gets us one value, the mean ERP amplitude, per trial: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_trials <- aggregate( roi ~ epoch + event_type + epoch_labels, dat_frame, mean ) names(dat_trials) <- c("epoch", "stimulus", "condition", "amplitude") str(dat_trials) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 'data.frame': 160 obs. of 4 variables: $ epoch : num 72 105 30 108 26 85 61 147 38 100 ... $ stimulus : num 41 41 42 42 43 43 44 44 45 45 ... $ condition: chr "car" "car" "car" "car" ... $ amplitude: num -9.97 4.8 6.69 -7.07 8.92 ... ``` ::: ::: We can make a quick box plot comparing the single trial mean ERP amplitudes for faces vs. cars: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(dat_trials, aes(x = condition, y = amplitude)) + geom_boxplot() + labs(x = NULL, y = "N170 amplitude (µV)") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](eeg-seminar_files/figure-html/dat-trials-boxplot-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: We’ll quantify this effect using statistical modeling in Vignette 7. Finally, we save the single trial data for later: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} trials_file <- here(deriv_dir, "sub-001_task-N170_trials.csv") write.csv(dat_trials, trials_file, row.names = FALSE) ``` ::: ### Building a Pipeline The seminar defines a custom pipeline function, combining all of our processing steps that we have done, with: - Input parameters: The EEG data (.set) file + all processing options - Return value: A data frame with single trial mean ERP amplitudes (as above) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} run_pipeline <- function(set_file, montage = "biosemi64", reref_chans = "average", reref_exclude = c("HEOG_left", "HEOG_right", "VEOG_lower"), filter_low_freq = 0.1, filter_high_freq = 30.0, downsample_factor = 4.0, event_codes = c(1:80), epoch_labels = c(rep("face", 40), rep("car", 40)), epoch_time_lim = c(-0.2, 0.8), baseline = c(-0.2, 0.0), artifact_threshold = c(-100.0, 100.0), erp_roi = c("P7", "P8", "P9", "P10", "PO7", "PO8"), erp_time_lim = c(0.15, 0.2)) { # From Vignette 3: Preprocessing dat <- import_set(set_file) dat <- electrode_locations(dat, montage = montage, overwrite = TRUE) dat <- eeg_reference(dat, reref_chans, reref_exclude) dat <- eeg_downsample(dat, downsample_factor) # From Vignette 4: Creating epochs dat <- epoch_data(dat, event_codes, epoch_time_lim, baseline, epoch_labels) dat <- ar_thresh(dat, artifact_threshold, reject = TRUE) # From Vignette 6: Extracting amplitudes dat <- as.data.frame(dat) dat$roi <- rowMeans(dat[roi]) tmin <- min(erp_time_lim) tmax <- max(erp_time_lim) dat <- subset(dat, time >= tmin & time < tmax) dat <- aggregate(roi ~ epoch + event_type + epoch_labels, dat, mean) names(dat) <- c("epoch", "stimulus", "condition", "amplitude") return(dat) } ``` ::: With this, we find all `.set` EEG files inside our BIDS directory (including sub-directories). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} (set_files <- list.files( bids_dir, pattern = "\\.set$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE )) ``` ::: modeling data for a single subject, just to get a feel for things. Let us load the required packages: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(lme4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Loading required package: Matrix ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} library(lmerTest) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Attaching package: 'lmerTest' ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` The following object is masked from 'package:lme4': lmer ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` The following object is masked from 'package:stats': step ``` ::: ::: Then, we'll start with a simple student's $t$-test for the difference between `"car"` trials and `"face"` trials: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} t.test(amplitude ~ condition, data = dat_trials) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Welch Two Sample t-test data: amplitude by condition t = 1.715, df = 153.04, p-value = 0.08836 alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group car and group face is not equal to 0 95 percent confidence interval: -0.3280523 4.6469514 sample estimates: mean in group car mean in group face 2.6327129 0.4732634 ``` ::: ::: From this (unlike in the seminar), we conclude that for subject 001, face images (as compared to car images) elicit more negative voltages in the N170 time range. ### Linear Regression The N170 `amplitude` is predicted by an intercept and the `condition` effect (faces vs. cars) The intercept is the average N170 voltage in car trials. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mod <- lm(amplitude ~ condition, dat_trials) summary(mod) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: lm(formula = amplitude ~ condition, data = dat_trials) Residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -46.734 -3.551 0.381 4.241 20.059 Coefficients: Estimate Std. We will apply our methods to the `dat_group` data frame from last section. We'll load it: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} group_file <- here(bids_dir, "derivatives/eegUtils/group_task-N170_trials.csv") dat_group <- read.csv(group_file) head(dat_group) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` participant epoch stimulus condition amplitude 1 1 72 41 car 0.529240 2 1 105 41 car 2.105713 3 1 30 42 car 6.097467 4 1 108 42 car 1.163520 5 1 26 43 car 5.642192 6 1 85 43 car 3.326762 ``` ::: ::: In our model formula, we want to capture fixed intercept and predictor effects *across* subjects. This requires some wrangling of the data: we want a data frame with a column of electrode names and a vector of amplitudes. The following code block does this in the `tidyverse` style: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_epo %>% as.data.frame() %>% filter(time >= tmin & time < tmax) %>% select(-c(time, epoch, participant_id, recording, event_type)) %>% pivot_longer(-epoch_labels, names_to = "electrode", values_to = "amplitude") %>% group_by(electrode, epoch_labels) %>% summarize(amplitude = mean(amplitude), .groups = "drop") %>% group_split(epoch_labels) -> dats_topo head(dats_topo[[1]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 3 electrode epoch_labels amplitude 1 C3 car 0.107 2 C4 car -1.51 3 C5 car 3.55 4 C6 car -0.935 5 CPz car -1.42 6 Cz car -0.778 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} head(dats_topo[[2]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 3 electrode epoch_labels amplitude 1 C3 face 1.57 2 C4 face 0.864 3 C5 face 0.453 4 C6 face 0.928 5 CPz face 2.74 6 Cz face 2.48 ``` ::: ::: We can then create a new data frame that has the difference between face amplitudes and car amplitudes: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dat_topo <- data.frame( electrode = dats_topo[[1]]$electrode, amplitude = dats_topo[[2]]$amplitude - dats_topo[[1]]$amplitude ) head(dat_topo) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` electrode amplitude 1 C3 1.466301 2 C4 2.378729 3 C5 -3.098379 4 C6 1.863789 5 CPz 4.158038 6 Cz 3.254394 ``` ::: ::: We can then create the topographic plot with `eegUtils`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Arrange data frame to account for bug in topoplot dat_topo <- dat_topo %>% filter(!electrode %in% c("HEOG_left", "HEOG_right", "VEOG_lower")) topoplot(dat_topo, limits = c(-6.0, 6.0)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Attempting to add standard electrode locations... ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Plotting head r 95 mm ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](eeg-seminar_files/figure-html/topoplot-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
